title: Adaptive streaming retry dampener and tenant signalization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers reported repeated 5xx spikes and downstream timeouts during long-lived streaming requests (chat + tool-calls) that coincided with background tenant maintenance and autoscaler churn. Root cause appears to be an interaction between our front-door retry policy and per-tenant admission signals: when a streaming RPC stalled briefly, the edge retried the request without signaling the backends, which led to duplicate inflight streams, KV cache churn, and cascading timeouts. This ticket implements an adaptive retry dampener for streaming RPCs plus an explicit tenant-level signal to prevent duplicate inflight streaming attempts while maintenance windows or reshard operations are in progress.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New dampener prevents immediate retry for streaming RPCs for a configurable grace window (default 5s) and reduces duplicate inflight streams by >90% in synthetic replay. 2) Tenant signal header is honored by all runtime pools; when set, front-door routing will fast-fail new streaming attempts to a tenant undergoing maintenance. 3) No regression in short RPC latency (95th/99th percentiles). 4) End-to-end test and canary rollout documented and run on dedicated tenants.
implementation_summary: - Add 'Stream-Retry-Dampener' middleware in edge gateway that tracks streaming call signatures and enforces a short backoff window before allowing a retry. - Introduce optional header 'X-Tenant-Maintenance' emitted by control plane during reshard/maintenance. - Runtime pools check header and surface a 409-fast-fail when maintenance is active; SDKs will surface structured error to enable client-side retry strategies. - Add e2e integration tests that simulate reshard + high fanout streaming to measure duplicate inflight suppression. - Instrumentation: tracing span and metric 'stream_duplicate_suppressed' and dashboard panel.
risks: - If dampener window too long, some legitimate retries may be delayed causing client-perceived latency; mitigation: window is configurable by tenant tier. - Header propagation requires small control-plane change; mismatch could cause unexpected fast-fails for some Dedicated deployments. - Potential interactions with SDK idempotency tokens for non-streaming calls; tests required.
rollback_plan: - Rollback edge middleware toggle (feature flag) to restore previous retry semantics. - If header rollout causes problems, disable control-plane emission of X-Tenant-Maintenance for affected region/tenant while monitoring. - Run quick canary downgrade to previous runtime image if downstream regressions detected.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem call with EPD and SEs. Reproduced duplicated streaming inflight behaviour locally by forcing front-door to retry streaming RPC on 502. Noted KV cache eviction spikes in the runtime logs.

2025-02-20 - Marcus Chen: Prototype implementation for middleware completed (edge middleware + small store to fingerprint active streams). Initial local replay reduces duplicates by ~85% but introduced rare 408s when grace window was 10s.

2025-02-24 - Kelsey Rivera (SRE): Added metrics and prometheus counters; found that tenant reshard windows correlate with CPU spikes and slower ACKs which amplified retry amplification. Suggested 5s default window and tenant-tier override.
2025-02-27 - Marcus Chen: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12879. CI passed except one flaky integration test; investigating flake caused by mocked network timing.
2025-03-01 - Product (Daniel Park): Drafted customer comms for impacted customers offering 1:1 support and explaining safe fallback behavior. CS asked for a rollback playbook—we added to rollout doc.

2025-03-03 - QA (Priya Singh): Canary on 3 internal tenants for 24h showed double inflight events decreased by 92%, no increase in 95p latency on non-streaming paths. One dedicated region reported an unexpected 409 spike; traced to control-plane header not yet deployed there.

2025-03-04 - Marcus Chen: Adjusted control-plane rollout to skip legacy Dedicated clusters and added compatibility flag. Preparing for In Review and merge. Test plan and rollback steps attached to PR.
